skill.name: sragent
skill.description: Query SRA and GEO accessions with SRAgent, retrieve related publications, and analyze genomics metadata for sequencing experiments.
skill.summary: Use SRAgent to convert accessions, inspect SRA metadata, and retrieve genomics papers.
skill.author: ArcInstitute

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are benign setup examples, Markdown code fences, normal Claude skill paths, or public genomics database references. Confirmed risks remain around secret exposure guidance, command-line API key handling, unpinned remote installation, and extensive external command workflows.

remediation.issue: Secret values can be printed or pasted into chat.
remediation.suggestion: Replace echo, env grep, and cat .env checks with presence-only checks. Tell users to configure secrets outside chat.

remediation.issue: CORE_API_KEY is passed as a command-line argument.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer environment variables, a protected config file, or a secret manager that avoids exposing expanded values in process listings.

remediation.issue: Installation uses an unpinned GitHub clone and local package install.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a release tag or commit hash and document verification steps before running installation commands.

remediation.issue: The skill runs external commands that access networks and write files.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation for installs, downloads, large batches, and output paths. Keep writes inside the workspace when possible.

content.value_statement: SRA and GEO research often requires manual accession conversion, metadata checks, and paper lookup. This skill guides SRAgent workflows for dataset analysis, downloads, and single-cell sequencing review.
actual_capabilities: Converts GEO, SRA, ENA, and BioProject accessions between study, experiment, and run formats.
Queries SRA and GEO metadata for organism, platform, library strategy, tissue, and cell type details.
Identifies single-cell RNA-seq technologies such as 10X Genomics, Smart-seq, Drop-seq, and inDrop.
Finds PubMed links, DOI records, and open access manuscript downloads for SRA-linked datasets.
Supports CSV batch workflows for accession lists and metadata enrichment.
Uses BigQuery when Google Cloud credentials are available, with Entrez fallback guidance.
limitations: Requires a local SRAgent installation and Python 3.11 or newer.
Some workflows need API keys for LLM providers, NCBI, CORE, or Google Cloud.
Paper retrieval depends on open access availability and third-party service behavior.
Results can vary with SRA, GEO, PubMed, BigQuery, and publisher network availability.

use_cases.title: Convert Accessions for Dataset Review
use_cases.description: Convert GSE, SRP, PRJNA, SRX, and SRR identifiers before deeper analysis.

use_cases.title: Validate Single-Cell Experiment Metadata
use_cases.description: Check organism, platform, library preparation, and single-cell technology for sequencing experiments.

use_cases.title: Collect Papers for SRA Studies
use_cases.description: Find linked publications, extract DOI information, and download available manuscripts for accession lists.

prompt_templates.title: Convert One Accession
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner lookup for one dataset identifier.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert GSE121737 to SRX accessions and explain the relationship between the identifiers.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Experiment Metadata
prompt_templates.scenario: Inspect one SRA experiment before analysis.
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize SRX4967527 with organism, sequencing platform, library strategy, and likely assay type.

prompt_templates.title: Find Dataset Publications
prompt_templates.scenario: Connect a study accession to literature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find publications linked to PRJNA498286 and report PubMed IDs, DOI status, and available manuscript downloads.

prompt_templates.title: Batch Annotate a Study
prompt_templates.prompt: For all SRX accessions from GSE196830, create a metadata table with technology, organism, paper links, and download status.

output: The result lists the SRA study linked to the GEO series.
It then lists related SRX experiment accessions for downstream metadata checks.
The response explains how GEO, SRA study, experiment, and run identifiers relate.
The response summarizes evidence from SRA metadata and study descriptions.
It identifies likely library preparation technology and sequencing platform.
It notes uncertainty when metadata fields are incomplete or conflicting.

output_examples.input: Download papers for accessions in a CSV file.
output: The workflow checks the accession column and runs SRAgent paper retrieval.
The result reports PubMed IDs, DOI values, download paths, and failures.
It keeps unavailable or paywalled papers separate from successful downloads.

best_practices: Confirm SRAgent is installed before running accession or paper workflows.

anti_patterns: Do not paste API keys, service account files, or .env contents into chat.

faq.question: What databases does this skill help query?
faq.answer: It focuses on SRA, GEO, ENA-related accessions, PubMed links, and related genomics metadata sources.

faq.question: Does this skill install SRAgent automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides setup and command guidance for a local SRAgent installation.

faq.question: Which API keys may be needed?
faq.answer: OpenAI or Anthropic keys may be needed for model calls. NCBI, CORE, and Google Cloud keys are optional for some workflows.

faq.question: Can it work without BigQuery?

faq.question: Can it download every linked paper?
faq.answer: No. Downloads depend on open access availability, publisher access, and third-party service limits.

faq.question: Is this only for single-cell RNA-seq?
